hook: The 'OK' hand gesture isn't universally positive.
fact: While it signals approval in much of the English-speaking world, the same gesture is considered offensive or vulgar in parts of Brazil, Germany, and the Middle East.

hook: Chess originated in India, not Europe.
fact: Chess evolved from a game called chaturanga in India around the 6th century CE, later spreading through Persia and the Islamic world before reaching Europe.

hook: Tipping isn't a global custom.
fact: In Japan and South Korea, tipping can actually be seen as confusing or even rude, since excellent service is considered a standard part of the job rather than something to reward extra.

hook: The world's most spoken native language isn't English.
fact: Mandarin Chinese has the most native speakers of any language in the world, followed by Spanish — English ranks third for native speakers, though it leads for total speakers including second-language learners.

hook: Handshakes may have started as a trust gesture.
fact: One theory traces the handshake to ancient Greece, where extending an empty right hand showed you weren't concealing a weapon.

hook: There are more Lego figures than people on Earth.
fact: Lego produces so many minifigures each year that estimates suggest their total population has long since surpassed the human population of the planet.

hook: Sushi wasn't originally eaten fresh.
fact: Early forms of sushi in Southeast Asia and Japan used fermented rice as a preservative to store fish for months — eating the rice alongside the fish came much later.

hook: Some cultures count age differently.
fact: Traditional Korean age counting considered a baby one year old at birth, adding another year every New Year's Day rather than on the individual's birthday — South Korea officially switched to international age counting in 2023.

hook: The white wedding dress is a relatively modern trend.
fact: Brides wore all kinds of colors for centuries; the white wedding dress became fashionable largely after Queen Victoria wore one for her 1840 wedding.

hook: Emoji started as a way to save space on pagers.
fact: Emoji were created in 1999 by Shigetaka Kurita for Japanese mobile carriers, partly to convey information — like weather or emotion — in far less space than text.

hook: Not all cultures nod for 'yes.'
fact: In Bulgaria and parts of Greece and Albania, a nod can traditionally mean 'no' while shaking the head side to side can mean 'yes' — the reverse of common Western convention.

hook: The number of languages spoken today is shrinking fast.
fact: Linguists estimate around 7,000 languages are spoken worldwide today, but as many as 40% are considered endangered and could disappear within generations.
whyItMatters: Each language loss can mean losing unique knowledge, stories, and ways of understanding the world.

hook: Fortune cookies aren't actually from China.
fact: Fortune cookies are widely believed to have originated with Japanese immigrants in California in the early 1900s and were later popularized by Chinese-American restaurants — they're largely unknown in China itself.

hook: Chopsticks were originally cooking tools, not eating utensils.
fact: Chopsticks have been used in China for more than 3,000 years, but were first used mainly for cooking and serving food from communal pots before becoming common eating utensils.

hook: A thumbs up isn't a friendly gesture everywhere.
fact: While it signals approval across much of the West, the thumbs up gesture is considered offensive in parts of the Middle East and West Africa.

hook: The Bible is the most translated book in the world.
fact: It's been translated, at least in part, into over 3,000 languages — far more than any other written work in history.

hook: Slurping your noodles loudly is a compliment in Japan.
fact: In Japan, audibly slurping noodles like ramen or soba is considered a sign that you're enjoying the meal, not bad manners.

hook: Piñatas didn't originate in Mexico.
fact: The piñata tradition is believed to have started in China, later spread to Europe, and was eventually brought to Mexico by Spanish colonizers, where it took on its modern form.

hook: Valentine's Day has roots in an ancient Roman festival.
fact: Valentine's Day traces back to Lupercalia, an ancient Roman fertility festival, which was later Christianized and renamed after a martyred saint.

hook: Using your left hand to eat is considered rude in many cultures.
fact: In much of South Asia and the Middle East, the left hand is traditionally reserved for hygiene tasks, so eating or handing something to someone with it is seen as impolite.

hook: Origami came to Japan from China, along with paper itself.
fact: The art of paper folding developed in Japan around the 6th century, after papermaking techniques were introduced from China.

hook: Clinking glasses during a toast may have started as superstition.
fact: One popular theory holds that the custom of clinking glasses began from a belief that the sound would scare away evil spirits lurking nearby.

hook: Yoga is thousands of years older than most people realize.
fact: Yoga originated in ancient India more than 5,000 years ago as a spiritual and philosophical discipline, long before it became associated primarily with physical exercise.

hook: In Russia, an even number of flowers is for funerals only.
fact: Russian custom reserves even-numbered flower bouquets for funerals and mourning — bouquets given for celebrations should always have an odd number of stems.

hook: Saying 'bless you' after a sneeze may date back to a 6th-century plague.
fact: One popular account credits Pope Gregory I with urging people to say a blessing after sneezing during a deadly outbreak, since a sneeze was feared to be an early plague symptom.

hook: Carnival celebrations predate Christianity.
fact: Festivals like Brazil's Carnival, held before the Christian season of Lent, trace back to pre-Christian spring celebrations that were later absorbed into the Christian calendar.

hook: Flamenco blends far more cultures than just Spanish ones.
fact: Though closely associated with Spain, flamenco developed from a mix of Romani, Andalusian, Jewish, and Moorish influences that mingled in southern Spain over centuries.

hook: White wedding cakes once symbolized wealth, not just purity.
fact: In earlier centuries, refined white sugar was expensive and difficult to produce, so a pure-white wedding cake was also a visible display of a family's wealth.

hook: The high five is a fairly recent invention.
fact: Unlike older gestures such as the handshake or bow, the high five is widely credited to American baseball players in the late 1970s.
